statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25 block threshold, because the CME weekend halt removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 64 in the elevated band on carried energy and policy exposure, and confidence is 87 on a complete verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Two independent facts support the reading. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion: the cash index closed 29,368.44, up 0.91% but 105 points below its 29,473.12 high, and NQ's final tick of 29,391.75 was 108 points under a 29,499.50 high. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly twenty-five hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No danger window is named, because a narrow evidence-based window cannot be placed inside a tape that is not trading. Elevated stress describes carried weekend exposure, not an active condition: an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage, a blockaded Strait of Hormuz, record distillate prices and a policy decision priced near certainty for Wednesday. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unchanged by this mapping.
headline: A shut tape into the weekend: NDX closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but 105 points below its high, futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC, and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage travels into a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range after opening at 29,331.48, and finished 105 points below its own high, so the closing auction did not extend the advance. NQ futures printed a final tick of 29,391.75, up 0.88%, some 108 points under a 29,499.50 session high and inside a 29,040.50 to 29,499.50 range. VIX closed at 15.84 after an 11.2% single-day decline. Participation was broad rather than narrow: delayed cross-asset context showed seven of eight tracked megacaps higher and the semiconductor complex leading, with several names up between 2% and 4%. Broad participation supports direction but is not by itself evidence of a no-retracement path.

The macro backdrop is the reason stress stays elevated while tail does not. August CPI, released at 12:30 UTC, rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over the year, both in line, while core rose 0.3% on the month, a tenth above forecast, and 2.4% over the year. Futures moved to roughly 87-90% odds of a 25 basis-point increase at the 16 September FOMC, from about 72% the day before. Yields finished the week at multi-year highs, the 2-year near 4.65% and the 10-year just under 5%, with the H.15 release for 10 September at 4.56% and 4.95%. Equities nevertheless advanced, and that combination of a hawkish rate path with a firm tape is a cross-current that raises stress rather than tail.

Energy remains the open geopolitical channel. WTI settled near $99.99, about 2.4% lower, and Brent near $104.42, roughly 3.0% lower, on reported diplomacy around the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed since late February. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, normally about seven million barrels a day and the principal bypass around the strait, was shut as a precaution after drone attacks on 10 September and had not restarted. The U.S. average diesel price reached a record $6.00 a gallon on Friday. Reporting indicates Gulf and Iranian foreign ministers are due to meet in Salalah, Oman, on Monday to discuss a temporary shipping arrangement, though the gathering is described as not fully confirmed.

All of that is carried exposure rather than live risk inside this horizon. The forecast window opens with the market already halted and ends at 21:00 UTC on Saturday, twenty-five hours before the Sunday reopen, so every slot describes a closed tape. Conditional tail therefore holds a residual floor of 5 to 7 that represents model uncertainty rather than any forecast of structure, and the dominant mode is published as normal throughout. Weekend developments, if any, would express as a single reopen print rather than as the sequence of failed retracements that tail measures, which is why they are carried in stress and named as checkpoints in the hourly drivers.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 22:00 UTC on 10 September to 21:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 15 with the mode mixed and eases through the overnight to a low of 11 as Asian and early European trade stayed orderly, with stress pinned in the middle eighties on the energy and policy backdrop. The mode turns trend-up from 06:00 to 11:00 UTC as the European session built a directional advance that still allowed retracement, tail contained between 13 and 15. The only watch-band readings in the whole window are 21 and 22 in the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots, both marked event/whipsaw around the 12:30 UTC consumer price release, where confidence also dipped to 70 and 80 while the reaction was still forming. From 14:00 UTC the mode returns to mixed and tail settles between 13 and 17 through the U.S. cash session, with stress decaying steadily from 82 to 72 as the session proved orderly. The final slot, 21:00 UTC, marks the CME halt: tail 7, stress 68, mode normal. No slot reached the 25 block threshold at any point in the 24 hours.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about twenty-five hours after this horizon ends. Conditional tail opens at 6 in the current slot, which is the only slot that contains observed rather than hypothetical structure, settles on a 5-point residual floor through the overnight and the middle of Saturday, then widens to 6 from 14:00 UTC and 7 in the closing slot as the distance between Friday's verified evidence and the eventual reopen grows. That floor is model uncertainty, not a forecast of structure: a persistent no-retracement price path cannot form while the contract is not trading, so the dominant mode is published as normal across the whole window and every slot maps to the same low-band policy state. Stress decays from 64 to a weekend floor near 46 by early Saturday afternoon and then turns back up to 52 by the close of the horizon, because the exposure carried through the weekend, an unresolved pipeline outage, a blockaded strait, record distillate prices and a near-certain rate decision, moves closer to being repriced in a single reopen print without any of it resolving. Confidence declines from 87 to 71 on evidence age alone; the underlying set is complete and verified, but it describes a session that keeps receding. No danger window is named, since a narrow evidence-based window cannot be placed inside a tape that is not trading, and the named forward checkpoints, Monday's reported Salalah meeting, Wednesday's retail sales at 12:30 UTC and the FOMC sequence from 18:00 UTC, all fall beyond this horizon and belong to later assessments.
